question: Which of the following comes in the category of plantation crop?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Coffee.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Plantation crops include** tea and coffee**. In order to thrive, they need** heat, humidity, and a lot of rain**. As a result, they fall under the **kharif crop group.**
 
• **Coffea** is a** genus** of flowering plants in the family **Rubiaceae**. Coffea species are **shrubs or small trees** native to** tropical and southern Africa and tropical Asia.**
 
• Coffee beans, the** seeds** of several species, are used to flavour a variety of beverages and items. The** fruits**, like the seeds, are **high in caffeine**, have a characteristic **sweet flavour,** and are frequently** juiced.**
 
• Coffee is traditionally grown in** India's Western Ghats,** which stretch over** Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu**. Coffee production is quickly developing in unconventional areas of **Andhra Pradesh and Odisha**, as well as the **North-Eastern states.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Potato__**

 __
 
• The potato is a **starchy tuber** of the plant **Solanum tuberosum **and is a** root vegetable.**
 
• There are now over** 5,000 different types of potatoes** as a result of millennia of **selective breeding.**
 
• The potato, like the tomato, is **nightshade from the genus Solanum**, and its vegetative and fruiting sections contain the** toxin solanine**, which is** toxic** to humans.
 
• Potato is grown in practically every state in India and under a wide range of agroclimatic conditions. In the **Indo-Gangetic plains of North India,** almost **85% **of potatoes are grown.** Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Punjab, Bihar, and Gujarat** together contributed to more than **80%** of total production.
 
 
 
• **Cucumber**__
 __
 
• Cucumber, (**Cucumis sativus**), creeping plant of the gourd family (**Cucurbitaceae)**, widely cultivated for its edible fruit.
 
• Cucumbers have a** poor nutritional value**, but their** delicate flavour **makes them popular in salads and relishes.
 
• It's a **warm-season crop** that's extremely susceptible to frost.
 
• In India, the cucumber season lasts from** January through April.** Cucumber seeds thrive in temperatures ranging from** 25 to 35°C**, with an average rainfall of **20 to 30 cm**.
 
 
 
• **Millet**__
 
 
• Millets are a category of **extremely varied small-seeded grasses** that are commonly grown as **cereal crops or grains** for **fodder and human nourishment** all over the world.
 
• Millets are major crops in** Asia and Africa's semiarid tropics** (particularly in **India, Mali, Nigeria, and Niger**), with developing countries producing **97% **of millet.
 
• This crop is preferred because of its **great yield **and **short growing season in hot, dry circumstances.**
 
• **Pearl millet **is the most extensively planted millet, and it is a** major crop in India** and** portions of Africa**. Other important crop species include finger millet, proso millet, and foxtail millet.
 
• With over** 7 million hectares of area** under cultivation, **India** is one of the **world's largest producers** of Pearl Millet. **Rajasthan** is the country's most productive state. The crop is grown for** two purposes**: human consumption and cattle fodder.
